claims.statement: Verified fact: BDO transfer cards expose a multi-party status flow involving the transferor, transporter, and receiver, including receiver acceptance or rejection.
Verified example: a Polish public procurement contract used weighbridge evidence as the basis of waste settlement and required each transport to be recorded in both the weighing system and BDO.
Hypothesis (unvalidated): private construction projects have enough mismatched cards, weights, and invoices to support paid proof-to-pay reconciliation.

contrary_evidence: BDO already records card states and retains withdrawn cards, so the product must prove commercial invoice value beyond duplicating the official register: https://bdo.mos.gov.pl/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/BDO_EWI_IS-Karta-przekazania-odpadow-wersja-1.2.pdf

Sophisticated buyers can specify BDO and weighbridge reconciliation contractually, as this procurement does, reducing the need for a separate platform: https://ezamowienia.gov.pl/mo-client-board/bzp/notice-details/id/08de7927-dcb3-b51e-056e-e50001ac1d37

economics.acquisition_route: Sell a historical three-way audit through environmental consultants, then convert the project to recurring proof-to-pay.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Unvalidated scenario: 15 active projects at PLN 3,000 MRR in year 2, 75 at PLN 3,500 MRR in year 4, and 140 at PLN 4,000 MRR in year 6 imply PLN 6.72m ARR. A 2.5-3.5x vertical-software value at 70% ownership can pass PLN 5m in years 5-7; inability to ingest evidence without manual rekeying after two pilots is a stop condition.
economics.founder_time: 3-4 hours/day for one waste class and one project workflow; use consultant channels for domain interpretation.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Hypothesis: 70-84% after connector stabilization; OCR and exception support scale with load volume and must be monitored.
economics.payback: Unvalidated customer hypothesis: one duplicate or overweight invoice plus faster project handover can repay a quarter's fees; validate on closed project data.
economics.pricing: Unvalidated estimate: PLN 1,500-6,000 per active project per month plus PLN 3-12 per cleared load; fixed-fee historical audits as entry product.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Waste movements and subcontractor invoices repeat throughout a project; evidence archives remain valuable at handover and audit.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: receiver/hauler exception histories and site-specific mass patterns improve anomaly detection; project evidence archives create high workflow switching costs
fingerprint.customer: Polish developers, general contractors, demolition firms, and industrial sites buying recurring waste transport and treatment
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: waste consultants, construction accounting implementers, environmental auditors, and paid historical-project audits
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: read-only BDO reconciliation, ticket capture, rate-card matching, duplicate-load detection, subcontractor exception portal, and final project evidence export
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: developer or contractor pays per active project and per cleared load when an invoice line is approved or an audit packet closes
fingerprint.problem_trigger: a load is invoiced or project acceptance is due while KPO status, receiver confirmation, and measured tonnage conflict

founder_fit: Entity matching, OCR, and anomaly detection fit the founder's data background.
The Polish regulatory workflow provides a narrow local wedge.
A retrospective audit can validate savings with low capital and part-time work.
Consultant-led distribution avoids dependence on constant founder networking.
risks: BDO access and automation constraints may force manual exports.
Weight discrepancies can be legitimate due to measurement timing or equipment tolerance.
Evidence errors could delay lawful waste movement or subcontractor payment.
Construction software and waste operators may already bundle this workflow.

structure.control_point: payment approval for a waste load only after BDO status, receiver acceptance, measured mass, and contract rate agree
structure.critical_dependency: timely BDO exports or authorized views plus tamper-resistant weighbridge, hauler, and project-contract data

thesis: For developers, general contractors, and waste subcontractors, reconcile each construction-waste movement across the BDO transfer-card state, vehicle, weighbridge ticket, receiver acceptance, contract rate, and hauler invoice. Produce a project evidence packet and approve only matched tonnage for payment. The official BDO record remains untouched; the business controls the commercial proof-to-pay step and charges per active project or cleared load.
title: Construction-Waste Proof-to-Pay Clearinghouse
uncertainties: Actual invoice leakage and administrative time per project are unknown.
Data ownership across developer, hauler, and receiver contracts needs testing.
The optimal initial waste category and buyer persona are unvalidated.
Project-based revenue may be less predictable than the recurring model assumes.
